game: TEN@HOU Week 4 2025, kickoff 2025-09-28 13:00 ET, NRG roof closed

script.base: Houston is -7.5 in a closed roof with a 39.5 total, so the book has HOU at 23.5 and TEN at 16.0. Base flow is Houston leading by the second half and closing with Nick Chubb (34 carries, 141 yards over weeks 1-3) rather than a shootout. Tennessee trails and has to throw more, but Ward is at -0.73 EPA/dropback vs the blitz against -0.09 unblitzed, Houston blitzes 30%, and LT JC Latham is out, so the extra dropbacks skew short and inefficient instead of into a track meet.
script.flip1: Tennessee hangs within a score. Pollard keeps the 18-carry role he has shown (54 carries, 197 yards), Houston cannot just run clock, and Nico Collins (25 targets, 262 air yards) plus Dalton Schultz (15 targets) see a fuller passing script. Both unders get tighter if the game never becomes a 16-point dog script.
script.flip2: Houston blows it open early. Chubb and Stroud late snaps are at risk and Woody Marks (12 carries, 44 yards) mops up, while Tennessee abandons the run and Ward's deep shots to Calvin Ridley (229 air yards) and Elic Ayomanor (241 air yards) either die on pressure or cash one garbage explosive.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse injury report only; inactives (~90 min pre-kick) are not in the pack. TEN T JC Latham Out (hip): pressure up, rush efficiency down, quick throws up. That helps Chig Okonkwo (16 targets, 120 yards, 69 air) and Pollard checkdowns (6 targets, 43 yards), and it hurts Ridley/Ayomanor deep yards plus Pollard's already 3.65 YPC. TEN WR Bryce Oliver Out (knee): not in the weeks 1-3 target table, so only a small bump to Ridley (21 targets) and Ayomanor (18). TEN T Dan Moore Jr. Questionable (illness): if he also sits, the OL hit compounds; not confirmed. TEN S Kevin Winston Jr. Doubtful (hamstring): missing safety helps Houston deep shots, chiefly Collins. TEN LB Dorian Mausi Questionable (back): if out, helps Schultz and Houston RB receiving; not confirmed. HOU CB Derek Stingley Jr. Questionable (oblique): if inactive, TEN outside WRs face a backup; do not treat him as out.

matchup.bleeds: Houston run defense is not the bleed: 4.34 YPC, 7 runs of 10+, and 20+ passes are 10 for 116 yards. The Houston bleed is the middle. Tennessee bleeds the run (5.89 YPC, 12 runs of 10+) and is soft on the right and in the middle; 20+ passes are 9 for 100.
matchup.overlap: Tennessee's cleanest overlap is Okonkwo's 4.3 aDOT into Houston's 8.75 middle YPA, but his 35.5 line sits on a 35 median and a 66-yard game that came with only 69 team air yards, so it is not a bet. The fade overlap is Ayomanor (13.4 aDOT) into a perimeter that is not bleeding plus a pressure/OL stack. Houston's overlap is Chubb into Tennessee's 5.89 YPC, but his rush line is his median and is not the selected leg.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both unders lost. On Pollard, Tennessee never trailed long enough to abandon the run, because Ward's -0.73 EPA vs the blitz made them protect him on the ground; Latham's absence cut efficiency but not the 18-carry role, and one 15-plus run plus screens pushed rush+rec through 89.5 the way the 92-yard game did alone. That counter still has to clear a line his best non-spike combo (60 rush + 29 rec = 89) missed, so it is not stronger than the read. On Ayomanor, Stingley sat, Oliver's absence added a target, and one of 241 air yards hit for a 40-plus gain against a secondary that has already seen 10 deep passes. That counter is the real one: if Stingley is inactive, drop Ayomanor. It is not stronger while he is only questionable and those 10 deep passes have produced 116 yards.
slip_story: One story: closed-roof slog, Houston -7.5 controls a 39.5 total, Tennessee's 16-point offense never gets efficient. Stack is Pollard rush+rec under with Ayomanor receiving under. They win together if Houston leads and pressure plus the missing tackle stall the deep game without a Pollard spike. Do not add Okonkwo or Ridley overs, a total over, or Collins over, which need the passing game or Winston's absence to turn this into a shootout. No TD legs. One market per player.
